headline: SILVER SURGES to $87.70/oz — Sixth Straight Annual Deficit and Solar, AI Demand Drive Historic Rally
snippet: Silver spot hit $87.70/oz on Wednesday, up 2% on the day and over 150% in the past year, as the sixth consecutive annual supply deficit collides with surging demand from solar panel manufacturing and AI data center buildouts. Gold held steady at $4,711.70 as investors rotated into silver for its industrial premium — the metal is up from roughly $30/oz in early 2025.

headline: COPPER SHATTERS COMEX RECORD at $6.69/lb; London Briefly Hits $14,000/t on China Demand Surge
snippet: Copper futures surged 2.4% to a Comex all-time record of $6.69/lb on Wednesday as Chinese demand rebounded sharply and supply concerns deepened — Peru fuel disruptions and Middle East sulfuric acid supply chain stress cited as dual catalysts. London copper briefly crossed $14,000/t for the first time since January's $14,500/t peak, with China's state trading company issuing a bullish 10-year demand forecast.

headline: BARRICK Launches $3B Buyback, Plans North American IPO Spinoff; CEO Says Newmont Fourmile Deal "Possible"
snippet: Barrick Mining launched a $3 billion share buyback after Q1 net earnings tripled year-over-year to $1.6 billion on a $4,861/oz realized gold price. CEO Mark Hill simultaneously announced plans to spin out Nevada Gold Mines and Dominican Republic assets as a separately listed North American company by end-2026 — and said an early agreement with Newmont on the disputed Fourmile high-grade deposit is "possible," which would clear the main legal obstacle to the spinoff.

headline: Uranium Holds Near $86/lb as AI Data Center Power Deals Fuel Nuclear Renaissance; NANO Nuclear Reports Tomorrow
snippet: Spot uranium traded near $86.30/lb Wednesday as the AI-driven nuclear power narrative continues to attract corporate capital — Meta's recently announced 6.6 GW nuclear deal with Vistra, TerraPower and Oklo is the latest endorsement of the thesis. Goldman Sachs forecasts uranium reaching $91/lb by year-end. NANO Nuclear reports Q1 results Thursday, with markets watching for updates on its microreactor development timeline.

headline: MITHRIL (TSXV:MSG) Drills 7.00 g/t Gold + 370 g/t Silver Over 9.65m at Copalquin — Resource Boundary Pushed 300m West
snippet: Mithril Silver and Gold (TSXV:MSG, ASX:MTH) reported hole RE26-009 intersecting 9.65m at 7.00 g/t Au and 370 g/t Ag — including 0.5m at 30.7 g/t Au and 1,780 g/t Ag — approximately 300 metres west of the existing Copalquin resource boundary. The intercept supports meaningful resource expansion ahead of a June 2026 estimate update, with 25,000m of drilling planned across the Durango district in 2026.

headline: WALLBRIDGE (TSX:WM) Hits Multiple High-Grade Intercepts at Martiniere Dragonfly Corridor — 4.53 g/t Au Over 13.5m
snippet: Wallbridge Mining (TSX:WM) reported initial 2026 Phase 1 drill results at its Martiniere gold project showing multiple high-grade intercepts across a 350m section of the Dragonfly shear corridor, including 4.53 g/t Au over 13.5m and 3.11 g/t Au over 18.4m. Results for four remaining Phase 1 holes are pending as the program approaches its May 14 scheduled completion.

headline: Gold Miners Poised to Finally Outperform Bullion in 2026 as Margins Hit Records Below $2,000/oz Costs
snippet: With gold near $4,700/oz and industry-wide all-in sustaining costs still below $2,000/oz, analysts argue gold mining stocks are entering a long-overdue re-rating cycle. The thesis: equities dramatically lagged the metal in 2025 (GDX +35-40% vs. gold +60%), creating valuation gaps that historically precede sector outperformance — Agnico Eagle's Q1 realized margin of $4,861 minus $1,483 AISC is cited as a benchmark.

headline: NdPr OXIDE CRASHED 21% in April to $99/kg — All Eyes on China's June Mining Quota Announcement
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium oxide fell 21% in April to $99.61/kg — its sharpest monthly decline since the Q1 rally — with NdPr expected to consolidate in a $95–$115/kg domestic range through Q2. The key catalyst to watch is China's mid-year MIIT mining quota announcement, typically released in June, which will signal whether second-half supply tightens or eases for the magnet industry.

headline: Energy Storage Boom Revives Beaten-Down Lithium — Battery Storage to Grab 31% of Demand in 2026, Up from 23%
snippet: A boom in battery energy storage systems has dramatically shifted lithium's demand narrative after years of EV-driven oversupply concerns. Broker Guotai Junan projects ESS will account for 31% of lithium carbonate equivalent demand in 2026 (up from 23% in 2025), with storage demand growing 55% year-over-year. The global lithium surplus is expected to narrow from 141,000 mt LCE in 2025 to 109,000 mt in 2026.

headline: HOT CPI + IRAN WAR RISK Amplify Safe-Haven Bid — Gold Near $4,700, Silver Charging Above $87
snippet: Wednesday's hotter-than-expected CPI print combined with escalating U.S.-Iran tensions created an unusually strong macro tailwind for precious metals and mining equities — gold holding near $4,700 and silver surging above $87 simultaneously driven by both structural supply deficits and geopolitical risk premium. Analysts note the dual-driver setup (fundamentals + macro) is historically bullish for junior mining sentiment.
